title: A Capped Doubling Game
problem: Flip a fair coin up to 10 times, stopping at the first head. If the first head occurs on flip k, you receive $2^k. If no head occurs, you receive $0. What is the fair entry price?

hints.text: Compute the expected contribution from each possible first-head time.
The probability the first head occurs on flip k is 2^{-k}, which cancels its $2^k payoff.

solution.setup: Sum payoff times probability over first-head times k=1,...,10.
solution.reasoning: For each k, P(first head at k)=2^{-k} and the payoff is 2^k, so that outcome contributes exactly $1 to expectation. There are ten possible paying outcomes. The all-tails outcome contributes zero.
solution.sanityCheck: The enormous rare payoffs do not dominate here because each doubled payoff is exactly offset by its halved probability.

keyInsight: A heavy-tailed payoff can contribute the same expected amount at every scale.
recognitionCues: A payoff grows geometrically while its occurrence probability shrinks geometrically.
commonMistakes: Forgetting that the no-head outcome pays zero or treating the ten paying events as equally likely.
followUps: What happens as the cap increases? Would you personally pay the fair price?

source.notes: Original finite version of a classic doubling-game family.
